notes: Every artifact EchoForge may download is listed here with an immutable revision, expected size, SHA-256, provenance, runtime identity, and retained license record. Nothing outside this manifest may be fetched by setup, and inference is forced offline. The runtime.* entries are the complete locked Windows/CPython 3.12 faster-whisper environment, including NVIDIA's pinned CUDA 12 cuBLAS/NVRTC wheels so GPU usability never depends on a mutable system Toolkit. Optional NeMo weights are kept separate from that environment and require the pinned Linux runtime described in worker-nemo; they are never imported into the Windows worker environment. Large publisher artifacts use immutable Git LFS/Xet content metadata where their per-entry provenance says so; smaller artifacts were downloaded and hashed locally. Production never uses mutable model aliases. Silero VAD is covered by the faster-whisper 1.2.1 wheel digest because that wheel contains silero_vad_v6.onnx. Model artifact profiles are independent of compute profiles, optional models are installed only on request, and a missing or unverifiable artifact fails closed before a worker can load it.

artifacts.provenance: The interpreter EchoForge ships with, so no system Python is required. python-build-standalone is the redistributable CPython build astral-sh publishes and uv installs; the install_only archive is the full runtime with the standard library and pip, and unlike python.org's embeddable package it can create virtual environments. Downloaded and hashed locally on 2026-08-07, from this exact URL rather than the percent-encoded form the release API reports, and both serve identical bytes; the digest matches the SHA256SUMS file published with the same release. The retained licence text is the LICENSE.txt inside the archive, which carries the PSF licence and the additional conditions for the bundled Windows components.

artifacts.provenance: Google's own quantization-aware-training Q4_0 GGUF, from the official google/ repository, pinned to commit 29d097773436b69ff9feafd636ab4cf873786537. The size and SHA-256 are the LFS object the Hugging Face API reports for that commit, re-hashed locally after download. The repository is not gated and the model card states Apache-2.0, which is a change from the Gemma Terms of Use that governed Gemma 3. The vision projector (mmproj-gemma-4-12b-it-qat-q4_0.gguf) in the same repository is deliberately NOT pinned: EchoForge summarises text and loading a vision tower would spend VRAM on a capability it never uses. The tokenizer and chat template live inside this GGUF, so they cannot drift away from the weights.
artifacts.runtime_version: llama.cpp b10298; Gemma 4 12B instruction-tuned, QAT Q4_0

artifacts.provenance: ggml-org's automatically generated GGUF conversion of OpenAI's official natively MXFP4 gpt-oss-20b weights, pinned to immutable commit ef9b12f2ff56c69cf32153a02784e7a3c88bf524. Size and SHA-256 are the immutable Xet object metadata. The pinned llama.cpp b10298 build post-dates native gpt-oss/MXFP4 and Harmony-template support; EchoForge never asks llama.cpp to download this model.
artifacts.runtime_version: llama.cpp b10298; gpt-oss-20b native MXFP4 GGUF / Harmony template

artifacts.provenance: The same release, built without CUDA, so the documented CPU fallback is a real pinned runtime rather than a hope that the CUDA build degrades gracefully. 18 MB, so pinning it costs almost nothing.

Official ggml-org/llama.cpp release build, tag b10298, which git ref/tags resolves to commit 15586e2d7165570fb3aa7c26e0d442e289ef69de. The tag is what the asset URL is addressed by, so it is what revision records. Size and SHA-256 are the digest GitHub's release API publishes for the asset, re-hashed locally after download. The CUDA 13.3 build is the one pinned rather than the CUDA 12.4 build because the target GPU is Blackwell (RTX 50-series, sm_120), which CUDA 12.4 has no kernels for; a 12.4 build would fall back to PTX JIT or fail outright.

The CUDA runtime libraries llama.cpp's own CUDA build needs, redistributed by ggml-org in the same b10298 release. Pinned rather than taken from the machine because the alternative is depending on whichever CUDA happens to be installed, which is exactly what this manifest exists to prevent - and the CTranslate2 stack Phase 2 uses is a CUDA 12 build, so a CUDA 13 runtime cannot be assumed present. Downloading it for local use is not redistribution; shipping it in an installer is, and that review is still Phase 6's.
artifacts.runtime_version: NVIDIA CUDA 13.3 runtime, Windows x64, as redistributed in llama.cpp b10298

artifacts.provenance: Mistral AI's own GGUF repository, not a community re-quantization, pinned to commit 74fac473c43357d7fb2671713608183cc72496d0. Size and SHA-256 are the LFS object the Hugging Face API reports for that commit, re-hashed locally after download. Q4_K_M is the quantization the architecture plan names for the bake-off, and it is the closest comparable to Gemma's Q4_0 at 8.24 GB against 6.98 GB - the difference in footprint is itself part of what the comparison is measuring. The BF16 multimodal projector in the same repository is deliberately NOT pinned: EchoForge summarises text, and it is a BF16 file larger than the whole quantized model. This model exists to be compared against Gemma 4, and is not EchoForge's default.
